summary: Applied the concurrency.md checklist (races, visibility, locking, lifecycle, state, counters) to the single changed file, SSTable.java. The patch replaces SSTable.delete()'s DATA-first deletion with an mtime-sorted deletion that uses FileUtils.delete(String). I also read the caller in LogTransaction.java (around line 401), where the tidier's retry-on-failure path depends on the delete throwing. Most checklist items do not apply: the patch adds no shared state, locks, or threads, and the local HashMap and list are not shared. The one real finding is in resource cleanup on the failure path. Not reviewed: nothing in the diff; the rest of the repository was only read where the diff touched it.

findings.rule: concurrency.md 22 and 19 (cleanup and failure path must match the previous behaviour); resource cleanup on every path including failure
findings.problem: The old code called FileUtils.deleteWithConfirm, which throws FSWriteError when a component cannot be removed. LogTransaction's tidier (LogTransaction.java ~line 401) catches that Throwable, logs 'we'll retry after GC and on server restart', and adds the task to failedDeletions for a later retry. The new loop calls FileUtils.delete(String), which returns the result of File.delete() and discards it (FileUtils.java:545-551). Trigger: any component delete fails (permissions, file held open on Windows, transient I/O error). The failure is swallowed, SSTable.delete() returns true, the tidier completes and the transaction is marked done, so the retry is never scheduled. The surviving component files are left on disk with no retry, and the failure is not logged at error level. The fix is to restore the throwing behaviour for each component, for example by calling FileUtils.deleteWithConfirm(desc.filenameFor(component)) in the sorted loop, or by checking the boolean and throwing when a delete returns false for an existing file.
findings.fix: In the sorted loop, use FileUtils.deleteWithConfirm(desc.filenameFor(component)) instead of FileUtils.delete(desc.filenameFor(component)) so a failed delete propagates to the tidier retry path as before.
